subject: Proof chaining & role assertion for portal onboarding
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@clearwave.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearwave.com
Date: 2028-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proof chaining / role assertion question for portal onboarding

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the onboarding kickoff earlier — quick technical question as we map evidence into Whistic and Archer. Our compliance team wants a clear chain-of-possession for artifacts that ties a Redwood portal upload (or API push) back to a claimed owner role and the originating SOC2 evidence. Specifically:

- Do you produce a signed manifest (hash list) that we can store in our system to prove provenance?
- How do you assert which Redwood user/role uploaded an evidence bundle (role assertion) when temporary service creds are used for upload?

If you have a short runbook or spec (manifest format, TTLs for ephemeral creds, signature algorithm) that would be perfect. We want to minimize back-and-forth with our InfoSec.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Senior Security Analyst
Clearwave Health

P.S. We can accept S3 presigned uploads or an API call — whichever you recommend for automations.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@clearwave.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-21T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proof chaining / role assertion question for portal onboarding

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front, then a proposed minimal runbook and attachments.

- Yes — we produce a signed manifest: a compact SHA-256 digest list (file name + hex digest + size) that we sign using our platform key (RSA-2048) and return as manifest.sig. That signature is verifiable by your team.
- Role assertion: when we provision temporary upload credentials for a partner-run stage (presigned S3 or ephemeral API token), we embed an auditable token (upload_token_id) that maps back to the Redwood user or service principal who requested the credential. The upload_token_id is logged in our audit events and referenced in the manifest metadata. That gives you an indelible link: manifest -> upload_token_id -> requester identity -> Redwood audit log entry including IP and timestamp.

Attached: redwood-manifest-signing-spec.pdf (format + example), onboarding-tempcreds-playbook.md (step-by-step), s3-presign-example.json (curl + example presign flow).

Proposed minimal runbook for Clearwave:
1) Clearwave requests an upload window (S3 presign preferred) and supplies the target portal profile id.
2) Redwood issues a time-limited presigned PUT for a staging bucket and returns an upload_token_id.
3) Clearwave uploads evidence bundle (zip) to the presigned URL.
4) Redwood ingests and computes digests, returns manifest.json + manifest.sig and links manifest to upload_token_id in the ingestion event.
5) Clearwave stores manifest.json and manifest.sig alongside the bundle in your system; your team can verify signature and confirm the claimed uploader.

Defaults we recommend: presign TTL = 1 hour; manifest validity window recorded in manifest metadata; signature algorithm = RSA-SHA256. If you need shorter TTLs (30m) we can accommodate.

Next steps: if this looks good we can schedule a short demo with your InfoSec to run through a sample upload. Jonas / Karthik — looping you in for the audit log / presign implementation details.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Vendor Security Manager, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-manifest-signing-spec.pdf (PDF), onboarding-tempcreds-playbook.md (MD), s3-presign-example.json (JSON)
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@clearwave.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearwave.com
Date: 2028-06-21T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proof chaining / role assertion question for portal onboarding

Marissa — this is exactly what we needed, thanks. Two quick clarifications before we lock the flow:

1) For the upload_token_id, can you expose that value in the manifest metadata (so our ingestion scripts can index it)?
2) We want Redwood to optionally sign a canonical manifest hash (manifest.sig) that we push into our internal evidence ledger (immutable record). Does Redwood support generating a detached signature (PEM/PKCS7 style) we can import into our ledger?

Also: procurement asked whether the upload events and manifest receipts are available over a read-only API (so we can poll ingestion status) versus only in emailed receipts.

If you can confirm those three things I can give sign-off to the onboarding ticket and we’ll schedule the test window later today.

—Elena
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@clearwave.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-21T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proof chaining / role assertion question for portal onboarding

Elena — quick technical confirmation from the implementation side:

- upload_token_id: yes, we include upload_token_id in manifest.json under metadata.token_id; the ingestion event (audit) stores the mapping requestor -> token_id -> timestamp. Example manifest metadata field: "metadata": { "uploader": "clearwave/portal-123", "token_id": "ut_8f3a2e", "issued_by": "marissa_cole@redwood.com", "issued_at": "2028-06-21T10:07:31Z" }

- Detached signatures: we can produce a PKCS7 detached signature (manifest.sig.p7s) and a PEM-wrapped RSA signature file (manifest.sig.pem). You can import the PKCS7 into ledger tooling or verify PEM with our public key.

- Read-only API: ingestion events and manifest retrieval are available via our Partner Audit API (GET /partners/{id}/ingest-events and GET /partners/{id}/manifests/{manifest_id}). We will grant your procurement account read-only scope for the test window.

Operational notes: presign TTL default 3600s (1h). For higher assurance we can issue single-use presigns (invalidated after first successful PUT). We log the client IP and SHA-256 of the uploaded object as part of the audit event.

I’ve attached the minimal API examples (s3-presign-example.json) and a small checklist for your automation team. If you want, we can create a disposable test integration (clearwave-test) so you can exercise the full flow without touching production profiles.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Portal Integrations PM, Redwood Inference
